note: A lighter, more modern answer to Cinzel; beautiful when tracked out for fashion, skincare and galleries.
weights_note: One cut. Caps only, lowercase maps to capitals.

note: Well drawn but a template staple; try Bigshot One, Elsie or Gravitas One first when you want the same mood less familiar.
Superb for width shifts on hover or scroll; thin weights fall apart below 18px.
weights_note: 100 to 900 variable plus italics. 200 to 300 for tall wiry headlines; 600 to 900 only at wide widths.
axes_note: wdth 100 to 200 is the reason to use it: tall and wiry at 100, wide racing-stripe forms at 200. It only goes wider, never narrower.

note: Fat sign-painter italic with real swing; good for food and summer brands.
Slab skeleton with pattern-filled stems; strongest at 100px in one colour, and noise at text size.
axes_note: MORF 0-60 reshapes the pattern inside the strokes, a good hover or scroll animation.

note: Compressed steep pen script with tall ascenders and strong thick-thins. Fits a long title in a narrow column, which scripts rarely do.
A warmer, inkier stand-in for Inter with a real black weight.
weights_note: 100 to 900 variable. 300 to 400 for text since 400 sets a little dark; 700 to 900 for headlines.

note: Lowercase is unusually readable for a blackletter. Tall capitals and long tails need the extra leading or lines collide. Never set it in all caps, because the ornate capitals turn to pattern.
weights_note: Single weight, served as 400.

note: A rare heavy oldstyle with real pen rhythm, and the italic is excellent. Figures are oldstyle by default, so switch to lining for data.
weights_note: 400-900 with italics. 400 for text, 800-900 for headlines.

note: Calligraphic skeleton and a true italic. Figures default to old-style, so add lining-nums for data; size up about 10 percent.
weights_note: 100, 300, 400, 500, 700, 800, 900 plus italics. 400 to 500 for text; 800 to 900 for headlines that still look penned.

note: True small caps with a swash ampersand; ideal for section labels, bylines and nav.
weights_note: 100, 300, 400, 500, 700, 800, 900 plus italics. 400 to 700 for labels; 900 for short headlines.

note: True small caps with a fat spiky ampersand. Use for eyebrows, menus and running heads instead of tracked-out sans caps.
weights_note: 400, 500, 700, 800, 900 with italics. 500 for labels, 800 for short headlines.

note: Reliable chunky slab but common in templates; tight apertures start to clog under 16px.
Counters shrink to bevelled slits, so words become black shapes. Superb at 100px, unreadable under 30px. Badeen Display is a tighter near twin.
Clean bridges and readable in sentence case, which is rare for a stencil. Shipping, hardware and field gear.

weights_note: 100 to 900 variable plus italics. 700 to 900 for headlines; 100 to 300 for tall quiet titles.
axes_note: wght only, smooth from hairline to black

note: Reads solid until about 60px, then a fine inline appears; keep it large or the detail is wasted. Small on the body, cap height 0.59em.
weights_note: One black cut plus italic.

note: Only works big: a beautiful column of pinstripes at 64px and up, gone below 30px. Needs strong contrast against the ground.
weights_note: 400 only plus italics. One hairline weight.

note: Proper Art Nouveau that stays readable; wine labels, theatres, tea brands.
Dense and crisp at black weight, with a looped ampersand in the italic. A fresh stand-in for the Tiempos look, added in 2025 and still unfamiliar.
weights_note: 300-900 with italics. 900 is the headline weight, 300 italic is the surprise.

note: The best-resolved straight futurist here: a and g hold together. Keep it to mobility, games and hardware or it turns to pastiche.
A low-contrast thin didone that stays light at huge size. It fades in grey ink, so keep it dark on light and pair it with a sturdier text face.
Anton with a full weight range, and the unflagged way to get that voice. Huge x-height (0.73em) so it sets about 15 percent large; size it down.
weights_note: 100 to 700 variable. 600 to 700 for posters; 100 to 300 for tall quiet titles.

note: One family can be both the compressed poster line and the wide label, which gives a page real contrast without a second font.
weights_note: 100-900 with italics. 300-500 for text, 800-900 for display.
axes_note: wdth 50-150, wght 100-900. wdth is the reason to pick it: 50 is ultra compressed, 150 is ultra wide, and both ends hold up, so width can be a design move or an animation.

note: Reads like a sans when small. At poster size the pinched joints, crossed Q and flagged 1 turn Art Deco. Includes Japanese.
weights_note: 400 only, and it reads as bold.

note: Neat drafting-room lettering. Right for wireframes, diagrams, annotations and sketchy product UI.
Covers compressed to wide in one family; animate wdth for hero type. Default width alone looks ordinary, so use the axis.
weights_note: 100 to 900 variable plus italics. 400 for text; 800 to 900 at width extremes for display.
axes_note: wdth 62 to 125: 62 at 900 is a compressed headline, 125 at 900 is a fat wide. Replaces Archivo Black and Archivo Narrow.

note: Upright letters with an italic pen memory, like a mathematician's neat hand. Very rare on the web. Comes with fine Ruqaa Arabic.
weights_note: 400, 700. Both work, 700 for headings.

note: Hand-drawn warmth with a beautiful looped ampersand; great for food, wellness and travel where a rounded sans would be bland.
weights_note: 100-700. 600-700 for headlines, 400 for text.

note: Letters built from round dots at display size. By about 34px the dots merge and it reads as a plain wide bold, so keep it at 60px or larger to show the effect.
weights_note: 400, 600, 700 static with italics. 600-700 for clear dots.

note: Modulated strokes give a bookish warmth without serifs. Museums, universities, NGOs.
weights_note: 400, 700 plus italics. Regular and bold only.

note: The strange one: hooked y and closed G read as pulp paperback sci-fi. One word or a short title at 48px and up, never sentences.
Over twice normal width, so one short word per line; stunning as a band of black at 150px. Needs fluid sizing or it overflows phones.
Fraktur skeleton drawn in an even line, like wrought iron; a very rare voice. Never set in all caps, the curled capitals need lowercase around them.
weights_note: 400 and 700. 700 is the display cut, 400 is a hairline that needs 60px and up.

note: A humane change from JetBrains Mono or IBM Plex Mono: open forms and a slashed zero. Wide set at about 0.63em per character.
weights_note: 200 to 800 variable plus italics. 300 to 500 for code and labels.

note: Every letter is made unmistakable, with a slashed zero. Health, government, finance. Replaces the two-weight original Atkinson Hyperlegible.
weights_note: 200 to 800 variable plus italics. 400 to 500 for text; 700 to 800 for headings.

note: Low x-height gives it a bookish calm that most sans faces lack, so size it up by 10 percent. Figures are old-style by default; 'lnum' gives lining figures for prices and data.
weights_note: 200-700 variable with italics. 400-600 is the useful span; 700 goes stout and friendly.

note: Made by averaging a designer's whole font collection, so the outlines look slightly melted. Human at text size, strange at huge size.
weights_note: 300, 400, 700 with italics, all good.

note: Wide-set mono with confident grotesque shapes and an unusually strong black. Its default fi ligature drops the dot on the i, so set font-variant-ligatures:none.
weights_note: 100 to 900 variable with italics; 800 and up stands as a display face

note: Looks built for cockpit displays: open forms, generous fit, no style. Strong for dashboards and readouts, bland as a headline.
weights_note: 400, 700 plus italics. Regular and bold only.

note: Drawn for aircraft cockpit displays: wide apertures and unmistakable 0, 1, l and I. Best for status panels and dense readouts.
Fat rounded sans with pleasing tight joins; great for consumer apps, snacks and merch. Covers Korean too.
Holds from hero down to button label with no fuss; strong for sport, logistics and tools.
Capitals throw huge looped swashes across the next letter. Title case on one or two words; all caps tangles into knots.
weights_note: 400 only; optical size changes the colour instead of weight
axes_note: opsz 16-72: 16 is sturdier and wider, 72 has hairline strokes and sets tighter. Browsers apply it automatically through font-optical-sizing.

note: Reads like plates and highway signs. Excellent caps label at 12 to 14px with 0.06em tracking. Barlow and Barlow Semi Condensed are wider siblings.
weights_note: 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 plus italics. 500 to 700 for labels; 800 to 900 for headlines.

note: Letters alternate solid and hollow for a hand-cut street-poster rhythm. Barriecito is the lowercase sibling. Festivals, food, music.
weights_note: One cut. Caps only, lowercase maps to capitals.

note: A better Baskerville than most defaults, with a swash Q and a handsome italic. Hairlines are fine, so stay at 16px or above. Figures are oldstyle.
weights_note: 400-700 with italics. 400 for text, 700 for headlines.

note: Caps only with a slab I, and each letter runs about 1.3em wide: plan on 8 to 12 characters across a full-bleed line. Let it run off the edge.
weights_note: 400 only. One weight, caps only.

note: Caps only. A slab I and oversized currency signs give it far more bite than Bebas Neue; use this instead.
weights_note: 400 only. One weight, caps only.

note: Fat tight lowercase with small counters, made for big brand statements. Turns muddy under 18px.
Good drawing, but it is the poster voice of every template. Reach for BBH Bogle, League Gothic or Antonio first.
weights_note: 400 only. One weight, caps only.

note: A geometric with soft calligraphic terminals. Food, family and community brands where Fredoka feels too childish.
weights_note: 400, 600, 700. 400 already reads medium; 600 to 700 for chunky titles.

note: Stressed strokes with a fashion-title poise. Beauty, perfume, galleries; pair with a sturdier text face.
Heavy serif with built-in swash capitals and curled terminals, part Bookman, part brewery label. Strongest in one or two lines.
weights_note: 400 only, already heavy

note: The real Clarendon voice with ball terminals, and the italic swings. It sets wide, so check long words on phones.
weights_note: 400-900 with italics. All of it works, 900 is the star.

note: A humanist stencil, not a military one, which is very rare. Bespoke Sans, Serif and Slab share its skeleton if you need a matched text face. Figures are old-style by default with no lining option.
weights_note: 300-800 variable with italics. 400-700; bridges get graphic at 800.

note: Copybook cursive with ruled guide lines drawn into every glyph, so words sit on a lined page. Holds across several lines at 1.4 leading, but clutters when small.
Heavy pen cursive with wet ink edges and plenty of personality. Its default line box is about 2.2em tall, so always set line-height.
A true black slab with tight counters, and a black slab italic is rare. Three to six words, never paragraphs.
weights_note: 400 and italic, both already black.

note: A thin serif stretched very wide. One word can run the full bleed. Words eat width, so plan for short ones, and it goes grey when small.
The best condensed gothic here: full weight range and a tall 0.8em cap height, so it looks big for its size.
weights_note: 100-900, all good. 300 is elegant, 800 is a poster.
axes_note: opsz 10-72, wght 100-900. opsz 72 tightens the fit for headlines, opsz 10 opens it for labels.

note: The open inline reads as neon tube or stadium signage at size; under 30px it clogs into grey.
weights_note: 100-900. 700-900 keep the inline open.
axes_note: opsz 10-72, wght 100-900. Keep opsz at 72.

note: Clean stencil breaks in a tall gothic; good for freight, workwear and event signage.
weights_note: 100-900. 700-900 show the breaks best.

note: A fat Scotch rather than a Didot: sturdier hairlines, so it holds at smaller sizes than most fat faces. Underused.
Bold at full width looks cartoon-strong. The wdth axis replaces the separate BioRhyme Expanded family, so load only this one.
weights_note: 200-800. 800 for headlines, 200-300 for an eccentric typewriter feel.
axes_note: wdth 100-125 is the character axis, plus wght. wdth 125 at weight 800 is the hero setting.

note: Proportional dot matrix that still reads as text. Grid cuts are the monospaced siblings. Skip the Ink cuts, their default palette is a gaudy rainbow.
weights_note: 100-900. 400 keeps the dots separate; 700 with ELSH and ELXP at 50 merges them into solid pixels.
axes_note: wght 100-900, ELSH 0-100 dot shape, ELXP 0-100 dot expansion, slnt -8 to 0, CRSV 0-1 cursive forms.

note: The best long-read screen slab in the library. Weight 100 looks expensive, and 900 packs tight.
weights_note: 100-900 with italics. All usable.

note: Fixed-width Latin that is far slimmer than Courier. Great for index numbers, captions and film-credit headlines. Full Japanese.
Korean headline face whose Latin has wedge notches that give heavy type a carved rhythm. Caps sit high in the line box, so nudge them in buttons.
Arabic and Latin drawn as a heavy broad-nib gothic. Blaka Hollow is a faceted sibling for layering; Blaka Ink has a fixed gold gradient.
Squarish bowls and a tight rhythm for motorsport, EV and hardware. A less-seen choice than Rajdhani or Barlow.
weights_note: 100, 200, 300, 400, 600, 700, 800, 900. 300 to 400 for UI; 800 to 900 for tight logotype headlines.

note: Pure Bodoni with an optical axis that takes it from text to masthead. Hairlines vanish over busy images.
weights_note: 400-900 with italics. 400 or 800 at opsz 96.
axes_note: opsz 6-96 is essential and must be in the URL. Force 96 for fashion hairlines, 6-11 for text. wght 400-900.

note: Drawn oversized: cap height is about 1.19em against the usual 0.7em, so use roughly 60 percent of your normal font-size and at least 1.5 line-height or lines collide.
A big sweeping Q and an italic that feels written. Oldstyle figures. Lovely for arts and publishing.
weights_note: 400, 700, plus italic in 400 only. There is no bold italic.

note: Condensed soft serif with curled terminals, a looped ampersand and old-style figures. Reads like a good hand-lettered menu, so it suits food, florists and small cultural venues.
weights_note: 100-700 variable, no italics. 100-400 is lovely; it keeps its charm at 700.

note: Upright French school cursive in a firm monoline, with letters that join cleanly. Line box is about 2em and text sits high in it, so set line-height and check alignment beside other faces.

weights_note: 200-900 variable with italics. 300-500 for headlines, 900 for fashion mastheads.

note: Wood-type gothic mass with a slight flare; best on short big headlines. Bowlby One SC is the small caps sibling.
weights_note: One ultra black cut, requested as 400.

note: Ultra-wide black slab with a fight-poster attitude. Short words only and check phones, since width runs out fast.
weights_note: Single weight, served as 400, reads as black. No italic.

note: Excellent, but it is what AI reaches for when told to be characterful. Only use it with the axes pushed.
weights_note: 200 to 800 variable. 400 for text; 700 to 800 for display.
axes_note: opsz 12 to 96 sharpens joins and ink traps; wdth 75 to 100 condenses hard. opsz 96 with wdth 75 at 800 is the cut worth using.

note: A high-contrast italic with engraved inline strokes in the heavy parts, visible from about 60px. A rare script that looks expensive and not like a wedding template. Title case only.
weights_note: 300-900 variable, plus a separate 1000. 300-500 is the best span.

note: Cleaner than Audiowide or Orbitron for sci-fi and automotive; Bruno Ace SC is the small caps sibling. It eats width, so keep lines short.
weights_note: One regular cut.

note: Reads like official print from a young republic. The italic ampersand is a sharp S shape. Good for museums, archives and law.
weights_note: 400-700 with italics.

note: Light flared strokes with visible pen stress; reads like a gallery wall.
weights_note: 300 only.

note: Built for signage, including stacked vertical setting. Inline, Outline, Hairline and Shade siblings are designed to layer.
weights_note: One cut. Caps only, lowercase maps to capitals.

note: A built-in drop shade gives instant sign-painter depth with no CSS shadow. Layer it over Bungee in a second colour.
weights_note: One cut. Caps only, lowercase maps to capitals.

note: Tight heavy headlines are excellent, but it is a default in AI landing pages. 'ss01' swaps in a single-storey a that shifts the tone noticeably.
weights_note: 100-900 variable, no italics. 700-900 is the reason to use it; below 400 it turns generic.

note: The SaaS hero look in one font. Competent, and only right when that look is the brief.
weights_note: 400 only. One weight, draws as a semibold.

note: Excellent soft display serif that keeps its shape in short paragraphs; good for food, hospitality and indie apps.
The best Cooper Black stand-in in the library: 70s warmth with crisp drawing.
A cool small-cap sans for labels, nav and table headers where Alegreya Sans SC is too calligraphic. Carrois Gothic is the mixed-case sibling.
A Trajan alternative with softer joins and fine detail at large sizes; open tracking suits it.
weights_note: One cut. Caps only, lowercase maps to capitals.

note: Softly rounded humanist sans with a faint hand-drawn warmth. A fresher alternative to Nunito or Quicksand.
weights_note: 100 to 900 variable; the heavy end is the best part

note: A clean, useful note hand and the reflex handwritten pick in AI output. Kalam, Mynerve or Reenie Beanie say the same thing with less mileage.
weights_note: 400 to 700 variable

note: Clipped corners give a hardware and HUD feel without the usual cliches. Games, robotics, crypto.
weights_note: 300, 400, 500, 600, 700 plus italics. 500 to 700; lighter weights lose the cut corners.

note: Charter with very wide language coverage. No fireworks, which is the point: it carries long reads and low-res screens.
weights_note: 400, 700 with italics.

note: Hand-cut condensed with an eccentric g, y and ampersand. Food, music and street posters; best at 40px and up.
weights_note: 400 only plus italics. One weight.

note: A neutral grotesque with some bite, and a solid unflagged pick when Helvetica energy is wanted.
weights_note: 100 to 900 variable plus italics. 400 for text; 800 to 900 for headlines, the black is the star.

note: A mono with real grotesque character and heavy weights that work as headlines. Its fi ligature collapses into one cell and breaks the grid; set font-variant-ligatures:none.
weights_note: 100 to 900 variable with italics

note: Wide didone with softened joins; feels like a hotel or auction house. Covers Thai too.
Well drawn, but on every fantasy and faux-luxury template. Weight 900 with its big Q feels less borrowed.
weights_note: 400-900, caps and small caps only. 900 is the less expected cut.

note: The Gotham look without Montserrat's stretched width, for brands that need to sound established.
weights_note: 100 to 900 variable plus italics. 300 to 500 for text; 700 to 900 for headlines.

note: The angular joins at heavy weights are the signature and also why it is instantly recognisable as template display type. Listed alternates do nothing in the served webfont.
weights_note: 200-700 variable, no italics. 500-700 only. Clash Grotesk is the narrower sibling if width is the issue.

note: The axis is the idea: letters lose mass by year, like an ice sheet. Use for climate, science or any story about decay, and keep late years huge.
axes_note: YEAR 1979-2050. 1979 is ultra black, 2019 is eroded, 2050 has almost melted away. Tie it to scroll.

note: The 800 packs a lot of black into a tight width; an Impact-style headline without the meme baggage.
weights_note: 400 and 800 only, with a big jump between them. 800 is the display cut, 400 is a plain text sans.

note: Comic Sans redrawn with discipline, as a full family. Works as genuine friendliness or as deadpan editorial irony.
weights_note: 300, 400, 700, all with italics

note: Axis effects are subtle and need 40px and up to show. A quiet way to animate type on hover.
weights_note: 100 to 900 variable. 300 to 500 for text; 800 to 900 for display.
axes_note: FLAR 0 to 100 grows flared stroke ends; VOLM 0 to 100 adds volume to the strokes; slnt -12 to 0. FLAR 100 at 600 gives an engraved feel.

note: Colour font: a serif blown up until RGB fringes show, like stained glass at 100px. It turns to soft mush under 30px.
weights_note: One colour cut, requested as 400. CSS color has no effect.

note: Two honest weights, so one family can run headline and body. Default line box is large (about 1.85), so set line-height.
weights_note: 400 and 700. 700 for display, 400 is a warm text serif at 16px and up.

note: The default AI luxury serif. Tiny x-height and thin strokes, so size it up. Under 20px it dissolves.
weights_note: 300-700 with italics. 500 or more on screen.

note: Caps and lowercase share one height, so a line reads as a single band. Rarely seen and instantly ownable for a wordmark or short hero.
weights_note: 300-700. 500 or 600 at display size.

note: Swashy italic forms on an upright stance. A better choice than a script for menus and perfume because it stays legible.
weights_note: 300-700. 500 or more on screen.

note: Very large x-height (0.6em) and a narrow fit, so it holds long text in tight columns. Pairs with Cossette Titre.
weights_note: 400, 700. Regular and bold only.

note: A narrow grotesque with a very tight fit, for headlines with a lot of words. Reads like print advertising.
weights_note: 400, 700. Regular and bold only.

note: The Courier to use: darker than system Courier, with true italics, drawn for screenplays. Instant manuscript feel.
Narrow marker hand with real gesture; fills a headline without shouting. No percent sign.
A solid book face and a stock AI editorial pick. The x-height is small, so set body larger than feels normal.
weights_note: 200-900 with italics. 300-500 for text, 900 is surprisingly fat.

note: Fine typewriter slab, paler and more elegant than Courier Prime. Fades under 14px on white. Its fi ligature collapses into one cell, so set font-variant-ligatures:none.
weights_note: 400 only, and light in colour

note: Inspired by Lagos danfo bus lettering, and it is unicase. Letters nearly touch, so keep words short and word spacing open. Unreadable under 40px.
axes_note: ELSH 0-100 (element shape) changes the notched edges of the letters and is worth animating on hover or scroll.

note: Cap height is 0.56em against Inter's 0.73em, so scale it up about 1.3x. Tight heavy weights feel like a fashion magazine.
weights_note: 300 to 900 variable. 700 to 900 is the sweet spot; 300 gets wispy.

note: Narrow 0.5em mono with charts in the font: {l:10,30,20,60,45} draws a sparkline, {b:10,30,20,60,45} bars and {p:35} a pie, live in text with no JS or SVG. Needs ligatures on, and screen readers get the raw string, so add an aria-label.
weights_note: One text weight only; there is no bold, because the weight axis does not reach the letters

note: One of the best black headline faces in the library; spacing is already tight, so do not track past -0.03em.
Lowercase forms drawn at cap height, so there is no case at all. Striking in short headings and logotypes; reads slowly in long lines.
Thin flared letters with a loose hand-cut feel and a sweeping N. Warmer than a Trajan type for galleries, wine and ceramics.
A condensed sign-painter cut with sharp wedge details on k and a. Give it room and a quiet partner.
White inline cuts make it read like currency or a stock certificate. Needs 60px to show them and about twice normal width. Diplomata SC is the small caps sibling.
Charming descending f and good italics, but now everywhere on AI-era sites. Stops at 500.
weights_note: 300, 400, 500 with italics; no bold

note: Well made and everywhere. Try Hanken Grotesk, Host Grotesk or Epilogue first.
weights_note: 100 to 1000 variable plus italics. 300 to 500 for text; 700 and up for headlines.
axes_note: opsz 9 to 40: use 40 for tighter display spacing.

note: Clean high-contrast headline that now reads as template. Gloock or Bodoni Moda say more.
About 37 percent of Inter's width, so it fills a tall narrow space like nothing else. Needs 72px and up to be read.
A monospaced Japanese pixel gothic that stays readable in sentences. Use multiples of 16px for clean pixels.
Monospaced dot matrix for counters, departure boards and receipts.
weights_note: 100 to 900 variable. 700 to 900 for legibility; light weights vanish.
axes_note: ROND 0 to 100 turns square dots round; wght sets dot size. Animate wght for an LED pulse.

note: Car-badge script with speed and contrast. Very low x-height (0.35em), so size it up, and never set it in all caps.
Letters sit unevenly like balloons; kids, games and onboarding screens. A short wght transition on hover makes it puff.
axes_note: wdth 75-100, wght 400-700. wdth 75 with wght 700 is the more distinctive cut, squeezed and tall.

note: The best free Garamond for text, and common on AI literary pages, so earn it with real italics and a good measure. Body reads best at 18px.
weights_note: 400-800 with italics.

note: Thick-thin stress with sharp wedges. Weight 800 hits hard and stays elegant, ideal for long-form headlines with attitude. Includes Devanagari.
weights_note: 400-800. 800 for headlines, 500 for sturdy subheads.

note: Best of the large Edu family: an Australian school cursive with real joins, four useful weights and full punctuation.
weights_note: 400 to 700 variable; 700 is a surprisingly strong headline

note: Flared Latin with strong contrast that reads almost like a serif, with Arabic for bilingual work. Caps sit high in the line box.
weights_note: 400 to 700 variable. 400 to 500 for text; 600 to 700 for titles.

note: Ball terminals on y, k and g give it a curled charm, and figures are old-style. Elsie Swash Caps is the showier sibling. Fashion, perfume, florists.
weights_note: 400 and 900. 900 is the hero, 400 sets cleanly at 16px and up.

note: A top Inter replacement with more snap in the heavy weights. Caps sit about 0.09em high in the line box, so correct button padding.
weights_note: 100 to 900 variable plus italics. 400 for text; 800 to 900 for headlines with real snap.

note: A single-storey a gives the whole face a modern zine voice. The light italic is slim and stylish, and 900 is a solid brick. Added in 2025 and rarely seen.
weights_note: 300-900 with italics. 900 and 300 italic are the two best ends.

note: Layered wood type with a built-in shadow and split serifs. It needs room; small sizes turn to texture.
weights_note: One cut. Caps only, lowercase maps to capitals.

note: Reverse-contrast capitals with ball terminals, a real show stopper at 100px. O and C close up under 30px, so check the word still reads.
weights_note: One cut. Caps only, lowercase maps to capitals.

note: The best working condensed in the library: true lowercase with even colour, so it can set whole headlines and not just short shouted words.
weights_note: 400-900 variable, no italics, no light weights. 600-900 for heads.

note: Sans with chiselled terminals and real gravity. Universities, foundations, law; pair with a quiet sans for text.
A sans with Didone-style contrast, rare in any library. At 700 it reads like a 1930s poster face; hairlines go below 18px.
weights_note: 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700 plus italics. 500 to 700 for display; 200 is delicate.

note: Distinctive a and g give an offbeat warmth, a strong pick for friendly but not cute.
weights_note: 400 to 700 variable plus italics. 400 to 500 for text; 700 for headlines.

note: 1930s show-poster contrast with italic r and s mixed in. Use for one hero line only.
Early 1900s German poster lettering with a distinctive M and n, and sturdy at text sizes. Underused; try it for museums, breweries and film.
Early 1900s flared lettering with an oddly proportioned G and a. Theatre, tea, spirits; keep it to titles.
Reliable UI face and a default in many starter kits. Fine when invisible type is the goal.
weights_note: 300 to 900 variable plus italics. 300 to 500 for text; 700 to 900 for headlines.

note: Slightly narrow with a crossbarred 7, a reserved northern voice. Finlandica Text is the wider body companion.
weights_note: 100 to 900 variable plus italics. 300 to 500 for calm titles; 900 for weight.

note: Solid coding face. => and != become arrows and math signs by default; use font-variant-ligatures:none outside code.
weights_note: 300 to 700 variable

note: Slightly calligraphic sans with old-style figures; a quiet alternative to the usual light geometric. Small cap height, so size it up.
Colour font with fixed grey gradients; CSS color did not change it. Looks like folded metal ribbon and needs a plain sans beside it.
weights_note: 100-900. 600-900 are best; at 900 letters widen into folded ribbon.

weights_note: 200-800 variable, no italics. 300 at large size is more unusual than the 700-800 everyone reaches for.

note: The workhorse chunky slab here; tidy enough for subheads and buttons, warm without being twee.
weights_note: 400 only, bold colour

weights_note: Single weight, served only as 50.

weights_note: 300 to 900; lowercase maps to caps; 300 is calm, 800 and 900 punch

Built from flat geometric blocks, like Josef Albers stencil alphabets. Default spacing is very loose, so pull tracking in hard.
Sharp spurs on a sturdy body with a very wide italic. A natural replacement for Fraunces when warmth needs an edge.
weights_note: 300 to 800 with italics. 300 is already sturdy, 700 to 800 italic is the hero.

note: Baseball-jersey script; a warm change from the usual aggressive sports faces.

weights_note: 300 to 900 with italics. 300 to 400 at high opsz for hairline heads, 800 to 900 at wide width for a heavy head.

note: Well drawn but the default answer for elegant on every template. Use 900 italic very large if it must appear, otherwise try Old Standard TT, Oranienbaum or Playfair at high opsz.
weights_note: 400 to 900 with italics. Regular is the cliche, 900 and 900 italic are the interesting cuts.

weights_note: 100 to 800 variable; 300 to 400 for text, 700 and up for titles

weights_note: 400 to 700 with italics, all good.

weights_note: 100-900 variable, italics. 400 to 700 do the work

weights_note: 400 only, already heavy

note: Roman proportions in a sans; pairs naturally with an old-style serif.
weights_note: 400, 700, italics. regular and bold with italics; no heavy headlines

weights_note: 400 only, bold italic colour

note: Confident wide neutral, the free route to the extended-sans look without a sci-fi flavour.
weights_note: 300 to 700; 300 and 700 both hold up

weights_note: 100-900 variable, italics. all usable

weights_note: 100 to 900, no italic.

weights_note: 200-900 variable, italics. all usable with italics; even 500 has swagger, 900 is a poster

weights_note: 100-900 variable. both ends work: 200 for tall numerals, 800 to 900 for heads

Sets small for its size with odd vertical metrics, so scale up and check centring in buttons. Natural for scoreboards.
weights_note: 300-700 variable. 500 to 700 best

note: Squared forms with chamfered corners; pick the condensed black end, because 400 at full width feels stock tech.
weights_note: 400 to 900; 900 at 75 width is the strongest setting
axes_note: wdth 75..100 and wght 400..900; animate width with font-stretch for hover and load-in, compressed black is the money shot

note: A connected retro script with flicked terminals, and a far better stand-in for Lobster. The zero is a bullseye that cannot be switched off, so keep digits out of it. Never all caps.
weights_note: 300-900 variable, no italics. 400-700.

note: Wide-set and gently modulated, it needs space. A classic beauty and hotel pick.
weights_note: 400. single regular; use size for hierarchy, never fake bold

note: Blackletter bones inside a readable roman. A way to say history or metal without losing the reader.
weights_note: 100 to 900 with italics. 300 to 700 give the best balance of strange and readable.
axes_note: opsz 12-72 and wght 100-900. fy and ff pairs touch at wght 900, so track out slightly there.

note: Range is the point: condensed to properly extended from one file, and the brand association fades once you go wide.
weights_note: 300-900 variable. 300 to 900; 700 to 900 are the fun end
axes_note: opsz 12 to 36, slnt -6 to 0, wdth 75 to 150. wdth 150 at 800 is a true extended headline, wdth 75 a tight one; opsz keeps small text open; slnt gives a real oblique.

note: Lively calligraphic forms with wide word spacing; covers Devanagari too, and carries more warmth than a typical italic.
weights_note: 400 to 800, five static weights; 800 for heads, 400 for short text

note: Neon-tube letters with a built-in 3D tilt, one of the few fonts made to be animated. Tilt Warp is the heavier solid sibling.
weights_note: 400 only; shape is controlled by axes
axes_note: XROT -45..45 and YROT -45..45 turn each letter in faux 3D; bind to pointer position with font-variation-settings

note: Engraved prism caps with serif detail; a still frame looks good, moving it looks expensive. Becomes grey below 28px.
weights_note: 400 only; lowercase maps to small caps
axes_note: XROT -45..45 and YROT -45..45 shift the facets as the letters turn, so it catches light when animated

note: Best pixel font in the library because the pixels themselves are variable. Stick to whole-pixel font sizes when using it small.
weights_note: 100 to 900 with italics
axes_note: wght 100..900, wdth 50..200, BLED 0..100 (ink bleed), JITT 0..100 (scrambles pixels), ROND 0..100 (rounds pixels); animate JITT and BLED for a live glitch

note: Sports family whose weights up to 600 are double-line outlines that snap to solid at 700; fine lines fill in below 26px.
weights_note: 100 to 900 with italics; 100 to 600 are double-line outlines, solid from 700
axes_note: wdth 75..125 and wght 100..900; sweep weight from outline to fill for a satisfying reveal

note: Sets like a mono with slab-like details; more characterful than most code faces at display size.
weights_note: 100-800 variable. all usable
axes_note: wdth 75 to 125. Width axis on a mono-feeling face is rare: wdth 125 at 800 is a wide stamped slab, wdth 75 fits data tables.

note: Bookman warmth with swooping terminals. Oldstyle figures only, lining-nums has no effect. A strong one-weight headline for anything that should feel 1970s and friendly.
weights_note: 400 only, and it reads as a semibold.

note: Caps are half lowercase: the P drops below the baseline and the M is rounded, which charms in title case and looks wrong in tracked labels. Allow for the P descender in tight stacks.
weights_note: 400 and 700 with italic; 700 is the one for headlines

note: A condensed sans with an opinion in every letter. Underused and very good for culture, food and small presses.
weights_note: 100-900 variable. all usable; 300 to 800 best
axes_note: opsz 12 to 72, wdth 75 to 125. opsz 72 tightens and sharpens for headlines, opsz 12 opens for text; wdth 75 is at its most characterful.

note: Monoline rounded strokes with a hooked r and wide word gaps, like a draughtsman lettering a map. Unusual for story-led brands.
weights_note: 300, 400, 500, 600, 700. 300 to 500 are most charming; 700 for heads

note: Ultra-narrow hairline; only earns its place enormous, filling a column height. Dies below about 32px.
weights_note: 400 only, very narrow and light

note: Letters have open gaps like a drafted circuit; a softer future than the usual angular tech faces.
A very heavy Clarendon with tiny counters and a wide set. One or two words only, and check that lines fit.
weights_note: 400 only, and that weight is an ultra black.

note: Rounded square counters at very wide proportions. Crypto-adjacent by history, so pair with warm colour or it reads as Web3.
weights_note: 200-900 variable. 400 to 800 best

note: Unicase mix of caps and lowercase forms that looks intentional and strange; tracked labels in it are a cheap way to look designed.
True Fraktur construction at bold weight.
weights_note: 700 only; a request without :wght@700 fails, so use the css given here

note: Wide slab with a built-in drop shadow, pure wood-type poster. Keep to two words, and the shadow clogs below about 30px.
Narrow hairline serif with a looped st ligature and a decorated em dash; use font-variant-ligatures:none and avoid dashes if those feel too precious.
weights_note: 400 only, light with fine hairlines

note: Thin narrow uprights and an italic that turns into semi-connected cursive. Use the italic for comments and pull quotes. Turns => and != into symbols by default.
weights_note: 100 to 700 variable with italics

note: Black compressed unicase with hand-drawn wobble; the poster move with more life than Anton, and it works at viewport-height sizes.
weights_note: 400 only, black

note: Dark text colour that holds up on thin screens. The black italic is a headline voice most sites never try. Oldstyle figures by default.
weights_note: 400 to 900 with italics, all good. 900 and 900 italic are chunky and calligraphic.

note: Terminal bitmap face. Set at multiples of 16px for crisp pixels. Its fi ligature collapses into one cell, so set font-variant-ligatures:none.
Flat-nib strokes with angular joins, one of the few scripts here that feels current. Survives all caps better than most.
Wobbly hand-cut capitals; lowercase keys give small capitals. Looks like a 1950s workbook title.
Fat flared letter with sharp wedges, a Cooper Black mood with more bite. One short line.
Extremely wide fit with long wandering joins. One short phrase surrounded by space; all caps falls apart.
weights_note: 400 and 500; 500 is the safer colour

note: Winky Sans with torn edges, reading like a lino print. The roughness vanishes small, so use it big.
weights_note: 300-900 variable, italics. 700 to 900 show the texture best

note: Slightly askew letters that keep working at body size, because the rhythm stays even. Better than most fun fonts.
weights_note: 300-900 variable, italics. all usable with italics; 500 to 800 best

note: Hairline condensed. Use very large on calm backgrounds; it dies on photos and below 36px.
Soft-geometric headline face with a close fit; Wix Madefor Text is its body partner.
weights_note: 400-800 variable. 500 to 700 best

note: Early-grotesque bones and generous word space. Good, but everywhere since 2016.
weights_note: 100-900 variable, italics. all usable; 300 to 700 best

note: Sibling of Sixtyfour on a 0.5em cell, so it fits twice the text per line. The scan-line gaps muddy below 16px; use SCAN 100 for small sizes.
weights_note: 400 only; the axes do the work
axes_note: SCAN -53 to 100 and BLED 0-100, same as Sixtyfour. SCAN 100 removes the stripes.

note: A high-contrast, Didone-flavoured mono in a 0.5em cell, rare and beautiful. Makes a caption feel like a fashion journal. Hairlines thin out below 14px.
weights_note: 400 and 400 italic only

note: Rooted in 1920s coffee-house lettering; lovely for food and small trades, looks dated beside glossy styling.
weights_note: 200-700 variable. 300 to 700 best

note: A set of cross-stitch ornaments, not a text font. Use repeated glyphs as borders and dividers, with aria-hidden. Yarndings 12 is the coarser grid.
weights_note: 400 only; dingbats, not letters

note: Flat-brush diner script that rides the baseline cleanly. Stronger as one confident line than stacked.
Heavy high-contrast serif with soft round joins; the strongest Playfair alternative in the library for beauty and hospitality work.
weights_note: 400 only, bold colour

note: Single-storey a and oldstyle figures give it the feel of a well-loved reader. It holds up surprisingly well as short body text.
weights_note: 400 only, and it reads as a bold.

note: A sans on Garamond bones with old-style figures. Ysabeau Office has lining figures for UI, Ysabeau Infant a single-storey a.
weights_note: 1-1000 variable, italics. huge range; thin cuts are stunning at size, 400 to 600 for text

note: True small caps for overlines, nav and credits; a far classier label than tracked uppercase.
weights_note: 1-1000 variable. 400 to 700 for labels; heavy cuts look carved

note: Japanese hentaigana font whose Latin is a strange brush-drawn all-caps alphabet. Capital T reads like a J, so test real words first.
Latin is spaced very wide by design, like characters on a scroll. Keep the air for titles or pull it in with negative tracking. Fits tea, ceramics, hospitality, anything slow.
Thick marker lettering with steady rhythm; it can carry a full sentence at text size, rare for a hand face.
Tight, well-made, Swiss-leaning grotesque; the swap when you want Helvetica calm with more polish.
weights_note: 200-900 variable, italics. 400 to 800 are the working range
axes_note: wdth 75 to 125. wdth 75 gives tight heads, 125 a calm wide; its Expanded family goes further.

note: A well-behaved extended grotesque in a full weight range; regular at large size feels like a fashion house.
weights_note: 200-900 variable, italics. 300 to 700 best; regular at big size is the luxury move

note: Latin from a Chinese display family, with square shoulders and a wonderful ampersand and 3. A fresh way out of Oswald.
Reads as a soft flared serif in Latin, with brush-like terminals. Uncommon and pretty for essays and tea.
weights_note: 400. single regular

note: Fine pen-drawn sans like careful notes. Beautiful for essays, diaries and gentle brands.
weights_note: 400. single cut; thin, so keep contrast high

note: The best rounded face here: soft without being childish. Wellness, tea, education, anything tender.
Latin is a warm Scotch roman with real presence, and it sets Japanese beautifully alongside.
weights_note: 400, 500, 600, 700, 900. 900 is barely heavier than 700, so there is no true black.

note: Tall striped capitals beside plain small caps, so words get a built-in hierarchy; set in title case. Numerals stay small.
weights_note: 400 only; lowercase maps to small caps

note: Chinese brush face with a heavy, charged Latin. No accented Latin such as é or ü. Shallow line box: descenders overflow it, so set line-height and avoid overflow:hidden.
Flat squared serifs with a tidy modern feel. The best general slab in the library and a good replacement for a sans on docs and product sites. Oldstyle figures by default.
weights_note: 300 to 700 with italics, all good.

note: Every glyph carries its own bar in the text colour with letters knocked out, so it is a highlighter stripe with no CSS. Tracking splits the bar into seams, so keep it at 0, and hold line-height above 1.2 so rows stay apart.
An inline cut runs through fat serif letters, which is rare and well drawn. The inline closes up below about 28px, so use it for a few words at scale.
weights_note: Single weight, served as 400.

note: Ball terminals and a swashy 2 give it a Scotch Roman richness. Drawn wide, so it takes up line length. Weight is the big untapped lever: hairline and black feel like two different families.
weights_note: 100-900 variable with italics. Widest serif range here: 100-300 for luxury display, 800-900 for loud editorial.
